# Rules

**Snapback 2 optimizes the edit-to-verified loop — the agent's building an app on it, and ours building it.**

Speed is the constraint. Everything below exists to keep the edit-to-verified loop short
and to stop this repository accreting apparatus faster than anyone can remove it. These
rules bind `snapback2/` and the LLPs numbered 1000 and up; Snapback 1 is baselined, not
exempt, and its numbers may only fall.

Each rule is **[check]** (enforced by `caps`) or **[review]** (enforced by a human).

## Budgets — every budget is a trade, not a limit

- **5 blocking checks, 60s total.** A sixth requires deleting one, in the same PR. **[check]**
- **59 documents in the working set** (`llp/current/`). Today's count. A 60th requires
  archiving one — which is just removing the link. Snapback 2 aims to leave this at 15;
  Snapback 1's links are archived at promotion. **[check]**
- **12 documents in the foundation** (`llp/foundation/`). **[check]**
- **This file: 700 words.** If it grows, something becomes a check or stops being a rule. **[check]**
- **1,500 lines per source file, baseline 204.** Generated files exempt — and generated
  files are built, not committed; so are benchmark run records under `benchmarks/runs/`,
  which are evidence, not source. The baseline is Snapback 1's oversize count on the day
  the rule landed; it may not grow, and `snapback2/` contributes zero to it. **[check]**

## Blocking checks

`caps` · `ref-check` · `snapback2/scripts/test.sh` · `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs --check` · `check-inventories`

## Loop shape

- **Every check reports all failures in one run.** Fail-fast is banned. **[check]**
- **Nothing blocks on anything slower than 60 seconds.** Slow verification runs on a
  schedule, attributed to the breaking commit, and files a bounded set of issues. **[review]**
- **Fix loops get 3 rounds.** Then stop: escalate to a human or descope. **[review]**

## Time budgets

Tracked every run of `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs` (appends `snapback2/metrics/loop.jsonl`).
A regression is a P0 with a name on it.

| | budget |
|---|---|
| Incremental rebuild after a one-line edit | 15s |
| Test what you just changed | 30s |
| Blocking gate suite | 60s |
| Full build, warm cache | 5 min |
| **`snapback2 check` on a program (the agent's product latency)** | **1s** |
| **`snapback2 doctor` boot-to-ready** | **0.5s** |

## Scope

- **`NOT-DOING.md` is binding.** Moving something onto the doing-list means writing why
  and taking something off. **[review]**
- **Delete; don't deprecate.** No compat shims or migration paths before promotion. **[review]**
- **Nothing is compiled, transpiled, or generated at runtime that could be built ahead of
  time.** **[review]**
- **A spec needs an implementer and a date, or it isn't written.** **[review]**
- **Only implemented specs bind.** A document with no running code behind it is a
  proposal, and a proposal cannot block a PR or justify a check. **[review]**

## Agents

- **Agents remove apparatus freely and add none.** An agent PR that adds a check, script,
  registry, config file, or design doc needs explicit human approval saying so. **[review]**
- **2026-09-06 session exception:** the user delegated the search implementation
  decisions; one `snapback2-core/build.rs` may generate pinned Unicode tables at
  build time, alongside the existing package build. No new gate, registry,
  runtime generator, or Unicode dependency is authorized by this exception. **[review]**
- **Snapback 2 LLPs are numbered 1000 and up**; `llp-create` must be told. **[review]**
- **Snapback 4 LLPs are numbered 3000 and up** (`snapback4/`, LLP 3000); it adopts these budgets
  and loop shape as its own and keeps its scope in `snapback4/NOT-DOING.md`. **[review]**

## Shared machines

- Warm, named lanes, one per stream of work. Never clone fresh; reuse the worktree.
- **Never `git stash`.** Use a temporary commit.
- Kill only PIDs you recorded at launch. Never by name or pattern.

//! One recognition of point keys versus prefix populations, shared by reads,
//! loop domains, merge discovery and program existence tests.
use super::*;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum Position { Page, Domain, Aggregate, Exists }

impl Binder<'_> {
    pub(super) fn is_page(&self, read: &ReadExpr, point: ReadMode) -> Fallible<bool> {
        let global = read.keys.is_empty() && self.catalog.tables.get(&read.table)
            .and_then(|table| table.maintained.as_ref()).is_some_and(|maintain| maintain.by.is_empty());
        if !read.order_keys.is_empty() || read.range.is_some() || read.matching.is_some() || read.filter.is_some() || !read.seeks.is_empty() || read.keys.is_empty() && !global { return Ok(true); }
        if global { return Ok(false); }
        // Speculation cannot emit setup or consume compiler names. The selected
        // form binds its key expressions exactly once in the caller's body.
        let mut probe = self.clone();
        let info = probe.table(&read.table, &read.site)?;
        let mut lookup = read.clone();
        if point == ReadMode::FilteredPoint && info.maintained.is_some() && lookup.index.is_none() { lookup.index = Some("byGroup".into()); }
        match probe.select_index(info, &lookup, point, &mut setup::Body::default()) {
            Ok(_) => Ok(false),
            Err(error) if error.code == "E_QUARRY_AMBIGUOUS" => Err(error),
            Err(point_error) => {
                // Only an actual index prefix changes the form. A mistyped
                // full key or an uncovered named equality keeps its point
                // diagnostic, including the established repair.
                let mut probe = self.clone();
                match probe.select_index(info, read, ReadMode::Range, &mut setup::Body::default()) {
                    Ok(_) => Ok(true),
                    Err(error) if error.code == "E_QUARRY_AMBIGUOUS" => Err(error),
                    Err(error) if error.code == "E_QUARRY_POSITIONAL_SCAN" => Err(error),
                    Err(_) => Err(point_error),
                }
            },
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn prefix_bound(&self, read: &ReadExpr, index: &ast::IndexDecl, position: Position) -> Fallible<(ast::RangeSpec, Bound)> {
        if let Some(range) = &read.range { return Ok((range.clone(), Bound::Literal(range.take))); }
        let ceiling = if self.caller_kind == ProgramKind::Job { snapback4_core::Ceilings::job() } else { snapback4_core::Ceilings::default() }.examined;
        let pinned = &index.columns[..read.keys.len()];
        // One group per distinct source key: a parent-scoped source cap bounds
        // its aggregate rows too, without copying a constraint onto the view.
        // A pinned unique key bounds the group as a cap does (wave 3 #7); `.id = x`
        // plans as the closed seek `.id >= x and .id <= x` on the next column.
        let mut equal = pinned.to_vec();
        if let Some(next) = index.columns.get(read.keys.len()) {
            let printed = |op: &str| read.seeks.iter().filter(|seek| &seek.column == next && seek.op == op).map(|seek| crate::print::expression(&seek.value)).collect::<Vec<_>>();
            let (low, high) = (printed(">="), printed("<="));
            if read.seeks.len() == 2 && low.len() == 1 && low == high { equal.push(next.clone()); }
        }
        let cap = self.schema.group_bound(&read.table, pinned).into_iter().chain(crate::bind::unique_bound::unique_bound(self.schema, &read.table, &equal)).min().or_else(|| {
            let m = self.schema.maintain_for(&read.table)?;
            let parent = m.parent_key.as_ref()?;
            pinned.contains(&parent.reference).then(|| self.schema.group_bound(&m.source, &[parent.reference.clone()])).flatten()
        });
        let bound = if position == Position::Exists { Bound::Literal(1) }
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.22 — ruling 24: the schema cap supplies the whole group's ordinary literal scan bound.
        // Queries with a non-uniform rule keep this existing capped path;
        // scan_at upgrades uniformly decided aggregates to streaming below.
        else if position == Position::Aggregate && self.caller_kind == ProgramKind::Query && let Some(cap) = cap.filter(|cap| u64::from(*cap) <= ceiling) { Bound::Literal(cap) }
        else if position == Position::Aggregate || (position == Position::Domain && self.caller_kind == ProgramKind::Job) { Bound::Meter }
        else if let Some(cap) = cap.filter(|cap| u64::from(*cap) <= ceiling) { Bound::Literal(cap) }
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.22 — ruling 23: only query loop and lane domains may consume a prefix under the examined meter.
        else if position == Position::Domain && self.caller_kind == ProgramKind::Query { Bound::Meter }
        else {
            let columns = if pinned.is_empty() { String::new() } else { format!(" by {}", pinned.join(", ")) };
            let mut page = read.clone();
            page.index = Some(index.name.clone());
            // @ref LLP 3000.036#13.3 — a synced table's horizon keeps the newest rows, so its page reads newest first:
            // the page rewrite and N_NO_HORIZON's window then agree, and applying both draws no N_SYNC_ORDER.
            let window = self.schema.table(&read.table).and_then(|table| table.sync.as_ref()).map(|sync| sync.horizon.as_ref().map(|window| window.by.clone()));
            if let Some(Some(by)) = &window
                && let Some(horizon) = self.catalog.tables.get(&read.table).and_then(|info| info.indexes.iter().find(|candidate| &candidate.name == by))
                && horizon.words.is_none() && horizon.columns.len() > pinned.len() && horizon.columns[..pinned.len()] == *pinned {
                page.index = Some(horizon.name.clone());
            }
            let order = if window.is_some() { ast::Order::Desc } else { ast::Order::Asc };
            page.range = Some(ast::RangeSpec { order, take: 50, cursor: Some(Box::new(A::Name { name: "c".into(), site: read.site.clone() })), site: read.site.clone() });
            let suggestion = format!("page with `{} N` and a cursor: `{}` (declare `c: cursor ?`)", if window.is_some() { "last" } else { "first" }, self.catalog.source.expression(&A::Read(page.clone())));
            // A filter pinning a whole unique key names at most one row: offer the one-row read first.
            let one = (index.unique && index.words.is_none() && !pinned.is_empty() && pinned.len() == index.columns.len()).then(|| {
                let mut one = page.clone();
                one.range = Some(ast::RangeSpec { order: ast::Order::Asc, take: 1, cursor: None, site: read.site.clone() });
                format!("`unique {}` makes this at most one row: `{}`; or ", pinned.join(", "), self.catalog.source.expression(&A::Read(one)))
            }).unwrap_or_default();
            let rewrite = if cap.is_none() { format!("{one}declare `cap N{columns}` on {}, or {suggestion}", read.table) } else { suggestion };
            let message = match cap {
                Some(cap) => format!("{}'s whole group has cap {cap}, above the {ceiling} examined ceiling; one read cannot examine the whole group", read.table),
                None => format!("{} has no cap over this prefix; this position needs a bounded page", read.table),
            };
            return Err(if position == Position::Domain && self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Query {
                Diagnostic::new(&read.site, "E_QUARRY_FANOUT", format!("{} needs a bound over the whole population it writes; an atomic mutation cannot page its fanout", read.table), format!("declare a real product limit `cap N{columns}` on {}, fitting the {ceiling} examined ceiling, or move this work into a resumable job (guide jobs); a first-N preview cannot stand in for every row", read.table)).guide("bounds")
            } else { Diagnostic::new(&read.site, "E_QUARRY_BOUND", message, rewrite).guide("bounds") });
        };
        if !read.seeks.is_empty() && read.order_keys.is_empty() && !matches!(position, Position::Aggregate | Position::Exists) && !(position == Position::Domain && self.caller_kind == ProgramKind::Job) {
            return Err(Diagnostic::new(&read.site, "E_QUARRY_BOUND", "a seek needs an explicit page bound", format!("{} first 50 by {}", self.catalog.source.expression(&A::Read(read.clone())), index.name)).guide("bounds"));
        }
        Ok((ast::RangeSpec { order: ast::Order::Asc, take: bound.maximum() as u32, cursor: None, site: read.site.clone() }, bound))
    }

    pub(super) fn check_meter_prefix(&mut self, read: &ReadExpr, scan: &Scan, aggregate: bool) -> Fallible<()> {
        if scan.take != Bound::Meter || snapback4_core::engine::rules::scan_visibility(self.schema, scan).uniform { return Ok(()); }
        let table = &self.schema.tables[&scan.table];
        let index = &table.indexes[&scan.index];
        let pinned = index.columns().into_iter().take(scan.prefix.len()).collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>();
        let used = snapback4_core::engine::rules::deciding_fields(&scan.table, table, &table.rules.read);
        let missing = used.difference(&pinned).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let mut leading = missing.clone();
        for column in index.columns().into_iter().skip(scan.prefix.len()) { if !leading.contains(&column) { leading.push(column); } }
        let mut page = read.clone();
        page.range = Some(ast::RangeSpec { order: ast::Order::Asc, take: 50, cursor: Some(Box::new(A::Name { name: "c".into(), site: read.site.clone() })), site: read.site.clone() });
        // @ref LLP 3000.028#4-put-the-rules-where-the-builder-meets-them — preserve the loop, callers and truncation cost in the reason.
        let jobs = self.call_chain.last().filter(|_| self.call_chain.len() > 1)
            .map(|(helper, _)| self.helper_job_callers(helper)).unwrap_or_default();
        let query_site = &self.call_chain[0].1;
        let declaration = self.catalog.source.declarations.get(&query_site.to_string());
        if aggregate && (self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Query || jobs.is_empty() || declaration.is_none()) {
            // @ref LLP 3000.036#11 — a total has no first-N repair (app-farm lane 087).
            let deciding = if missing.is_empty() { leading.join(", ") } else { missing.iter().map(|c| format!(".{c}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ") };
            let grant = snapback4_core::engine::rules::grant_decision(self.schema, scan);
            // @ref LLP 3000.036#17.8 — a readable grant the program requires before the total (`require exists staff[viewer]`)
            // makes every row readable for every caller who reaches it, which the server decides once (read.rs `granted`).
            let guard = grant.as_ref().map_or_else(String::new, |grant| format!("; or guard it with the grant, so every caller who reaches it reads every row: `require {} else …` before it (or `if {}:` around it)", grant.quarry(), grant.quarry()));
            let diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(&read.site, "E_QUARRY_BOUND", format!("{} by {}: a total over rows the viewer may only partly read is not decided by its pinned columns, so no page bound makes it exact", scan.table, scan.index),
                format!("pin {deciding} with where equalities so one verdict covers every row (the total then covers only that scope){guard}; {}. If the maintained count keeps the source's private read rule, its group keys must carry every field that rule reads (including {deciding}); a public total instead deliberately discloses the count across hidden rows; or return a `first N` page with a cursor and fold it in the client", self.total_view_recipe(read, scan))).guide("bounds");
            if grant.is_some() && self.caller_kind == ProgramKind::Query && self.call_chain.len() == 1 {
                self.pending_totals.push((scan.site.clone(), diagnostic));
                return Ok(());
            }
            return Err(diagnostic);
        }
        if self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Query || jobs.is_empty() || declaration.is_none() {
            return Err(Diagnostic::new(&read.site, "E_QUARRY_BOUND", format!("{} by {}: a meter-bounded prefix needs a read rule uniformly decided by its pinned columns", scan.table, scan.index),
                format!("use `first N`: `{}` (declare `c: cursor ?` and follow its cursor); for a complete read, scan by an index leading with {} and pin the deciding columns (N_NEVER_COMPLETE)", self.catalog.source.expression(&A::Read(page)), leading.join(", "))).guide("bounds"));
        }
        let chain = self.call_chain.iter().map(|(name, site)| format!("{name} (at {site})")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" -> ");
        let job = format!("the system job caller(s) {}", jobs.join(", "));
        let authored = self.catalog.read_origins.get(&read.site.to_string()).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| self.catalog.source.expression(&A::Read(read.clone())));
        let rule = if missing.is_empty() { "read rule".into() } else { format!("{}-based read rule", missing.join(", ")) };
            ir::var(&left_value)
        };
        let focal_nullable = |value: &A, ty: &Ty| self.in_predicate && ty.is_optional()
            && self.focal.as_ref().is_some_and(|(name, ty)| name == "$filter" && matches!(ty, Ty::Row(_)))
            && super::super::intent::column(value).is_some();
        let nullable_left = focal_nullable(left, &lt);
        let nullable_right = focal_nullable(right, &rt);
        let ir_op = match op {
            "/" | "%" => {
                if !matches!(lt, Ty::Int | Ty::Time) || !matches!(rt, Ty::Int | Ty::Time) {
                    return Err(type_error(site, format!("{op} takes present ints or times; got {} and {}", lt.name(), rt.name()), "narrow the operands before division"));
                }
                // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.1 — division shares divmod's Euclidean result and zero refusal.
                let divided = Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Divmod { remainder_sink: "operator".into() }, args: vec![l, r] };
                return Ok((ir::field(divided, if op == "/" { "quotient" } else { "remainder" }), Ty::Int));

const fetchIdentity = async (url: string, timeoutMs: number) => {
  const response = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) });

//! A prefix that pins a unique key bounds its rows as a `cap` does: at most
//! one row, or one per value of the key's remaining finite columns (`unique
//! subscriber, topic` with a three-value `topic` enum: three rows per
//! subscriber). The store enforces the key on every insert and update, so

// @ref LLP 3000.036#13.4 — wave 3 #7: a unique-key equality is a bound (lanes 041 058 098).
use snapback4_core::schema::{ColumnType, Schema};

/// The tighter of the schema's cap over `pinned` and a unique key's bound.
pub(crate) fn group_bound(schema: &Schema, table: &str, pinned: &[String]) -> Option<u32> {
    schema.group_bound(table, pinned).into_iter().chain(unique_bound(schema, table, pinned)).min()
}

/// Rows a prefix pinning `pinned` can hold under some unique key of `table`.
pub(crate) fn unique_bound(schema: &Schema, table: &str, pinned: &[String]) -> Option<u32> {
    let info = schema.table(table)?;
    let column = |name: &str| if name == "id" { Some(&ColumnType::Id) } else { info.columns.get(name) };
    info.indexes.values().filter(|index| index.unique && index.is_plain()).filter_map(|index| {
        let columns = index.columns();
        // A nullable key column admits tied nulls; and an unpinned column
        // bounds the group only through its finite set of values.
        let mut rows: u32 = 1;
        for name in &columns {
            let kind = column(name)?;
            if kind.is_optional() { return None; }
            if pinned.contains(name) { continue; }
            let values = match kind {
                ColumnType::Enum { variants } => u32::try_from(variants.len()).ok()?,
                ColumnType::Bool => 2,
                _ => return None,
            };
            rows = rows.checked_mul(values)?;
        }
        (!columns.is_empty()).then_some(rows)
    }).min()
}

  // Record their group too, so stop/startup cleanup cannot report success
  // before Vite plugins and other inherited descendants have left custody.

  const executableArgs = grouped ? [resolve(fileURLToPath(new URL("./proof-command.js", import.meta.url))), command, ...args] : [...args];

"pipe" : "ignore", options.secret ? "pipe" : out!, err, ...(grouped ? ["ipc" as const] : [])] }); }
  finally { if (out !== undefined) closeSync(out); closeSync(err); }
  if (privateGroup && child.pid) privateGroups.set(child, child.pid);

  let stdout = "";

  child.stdin?.on("error", () => {});

  let actualSignal: NodeJS.Signals | null = null;
  let startedResolve!: () => void, startedReject!: (error: Error) => void, startedSettled = false;
  const started = new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => { startedResolve = resolve; startedReject = reject; });
  void started.catch(() => {}); // command() observes close/error instead; host startup awaits this promise.
  const didStart = () => { if (!startedSettled) { startedSettled = true; startedResolve(); } };
  const failedStart = (value: unknown) => { if (!startedSettled) { startedSettled = true; startedReject(value instanceof Error ? value : Error(String(value))); } };
  if (!grouped) didStart();

    const event = message as {type?:string;pid?:number;code?:number|null;signal?:NodeJS.Signals|null;error?:string};

    failedStart(error ?? Error("proof command exited before its process-group handshake"));
    groupGone(child).then(resolve,reject);
  }));

  // Observe the promise here as well so an early frontend close cannot create
  // an unhandled rejection before its startup catch reaches stopChild().
  void closed.catch(() => {});
  return { child, logs, id, closed, started, pid: () => actualPid, code: () => grouped ? actualCode : child.exitCode, signal: () => grouped ? actualSignal : child.signalCode, stdout: () => options.secret ? stdout : logText(logs.stdout), error: () => error };

function validatePlan(options: SeedAccountsOptions) {
  // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#8-wave-18-developer-loop-amendment-dx4 — custom argument keys override defaults; the seat grants no extra authority.

  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(service) || !Number.isSafeInteger(timeout) || timeout < 1 || !Number.isSafeInteger(users) || users<0 || (!roles.length&&!users) || (users>0&&roles.some(([role])=>role==="users")) || roles.some(([role, n]) => !/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$/.test(role) || !Number.isSafeInteger(n) || n < 1)
      || roles.reduce((sum, [, n]) => sum + n, users) > 100 || (roles.length>0 || options.provision!==undefined) && (typeof options.provision?.name!=="string" || !/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)*$/.test(options.provision.name))) {
    throw Error("E_STAGING_INPUT: provide 1..100 accounts across named roles, a mutation handle and a positive timeoutMs");
  }

//! Assets on the wire: `POST /assets` takes the bytes and answers with the
//! asset's facts; `GET /assets/<id>` serves them to a viewer the home row's
//! read rule admits (LLP 1006 carried into Snapback 4). A one-view image is
//! served once per principal and never cached anywhere; a deleted, cleared
//! or expired home stops the bytes at the server. A `file` (LLP 3000.038)
//! is uploaded with `?as=file&name=` and its declared `Content-Type`, which
//! the server verifies against the bytes; it is only ever served as an
//! attachment under `nosniff` and a sandboxing CSP.

use crate::serve::{Shared, cors, RequestFacts, principal_of, refusal_json, respond};
use serde_json::json;
use snapback4_core::error::Refusal;
use std::io::{self, Read as _, Seek, SeekFrom};
use tiny_http::{Header, Request, Response};

/// The most an upload may be when no column bounds it yet: the request is
/// refused before the schema is consulted.
pub const UPLOAD_CEILING: usize = 64 << 20;

pub struct UploadPermit<'a>(&'a std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize);
pub fn admit(shared: &Shared) -> Option<UploadPermit<'_>> {
    use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
    shared.uploads.fetch_update(Ordering::AcqRel, Ordering::Acquire, |n| (n < 2).then_some(n + 1)).ok()?;
    Some(UploadPermit(&shared.uploads))
}
impl Drop for UploadPermit<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) { self.0.fetch_sub(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release); }
}

/// Whether `POST /assets` carries `as=file`.
pub fn is_file_upload(url: &str) -> bool {
    crate::serve::query_params(url).get("as").is_some_and(|kind| kind == "file")
}

/// The most bytes a file upload may stream: the schema's largest file
/// bound, under the general upload ceiling. A schema with no file column
/// refuses before any body is read.
pub fn file_ceiling(shared: &Shared) -> Result<usize, Refusal> {
    match shared.engine.call(|engine, _| engine.file_upload_ceiling())? {
        Some(max) => Ok((max as usize).min(UPLOAD_CEILING)),
        None => Err(Refusal::new("E_ASSET_TYPE", "asset", "no column of this backend takes a file; declare one (`doc: file <=10000000`)").guide("assets")),
    }
}

pub fn upload(request: Request, body: Vec<u8>, shared: &Shared) {
    let principal = match principal_of(&request, shared) {
        Ok(principal) => principal.0,
        Err(refusal) => return respond(request, 401, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&refusal) })),
    };
    if body.is_empty() {
        return respond(request, 400, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&Refusal::new("E_ASSET_TYPE", "asset", "the upload is empty: POST the file's bytes as the body").guide("assets")) }));
    }
    let params = crate::serve::query_params(request.url());
    let file = match params.get("as").map(String::as_str) {
        None | Some("image" | "video") => None,
        Some("file") => Some(params.get("name").cloned().unwrap_or_default()),
        Some(other) => return respond(request, 400, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("as={other} is not an upload kind; use as=file for a document, or omit it for an image or video")).guide("assets")) })),
    };
    let declared = match crate::serve::single_header(&request, "content-type") {
        Ok(value) => snapback4_core::assets::declared_type(value),
        Err(()) => return respond(request, 400, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", "send one Content-Type header").guide("assets")) })),
    };
    let intent = params.get("intent").map(String::as_str);
    if intent.is_some_and(|id| id.is_empty() || id.len() > 128 || !id.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'-' || b == b'_')) {
        return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied": Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", "intent is 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens or underscores")}));
    }
    use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
    let fingerprint = snapback4_core::value::digest(&(format!("{:x}", Sha256::digest(&body)), &file.as_ref().map(|name| snapback4_core::assets::sanitize_name(name)), &declared));
    let expected_store = params.get("store_id");
    if intent.is_some() && expected_store.is_none() { return respond(request,400,json!({"denied":Refusal::new("E_INPUT","input","intent uploads require store_id from the identified backend")})); }
    let facts = RequestFacts::capture(&request);
    let stored = (|| {
        let (intent, expected_store) = (intent.map(str::to_owned), expected_store.cloned());
        let (principal_check, fingerprint_check, intent_check, expected_check, facts_check) =
            (principal.clone(), fingerprint.clone(), intent.clone(), expected_store.clone(), facts.clone());
        let (replay, placement) = shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {
            if let Some(expected) = &expected_check {
                if engine.store().store_identity()?.as_ref() != Some(expected) {
                    return Err(snapback4_core::RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_STORE_REPLACED", message: "upload intent belongs to another backend store".into() });
                }
            }
            if let Some(id) = &intent_check {
                crate::serve::session_identity::mutation_authority(&facts_check, shared, engine, &principal_check).map_err(|why| snapback4_core::RuntimeError::Auth(why.message))?;
                if let Some(asset) = engine.asset_intent(&principal_check, id, &fingerprint_check)? { return Ok((Some(asset), None)); }
            }
            let placement = if let Some(id) = &intent_check { Some(engine.asset_declaration(&principal_check, id)?.ok_or_else(|| snapback4_core::RuntimeError::Asset { code: "E_UPLOAD_INTENT", message: "declare this intent's immutable placement before sending its bytes".into() })?) } else { None };
            Ok((None, placement))
        })?;
        if let Some(asset) = replay { return Ok(asset); }
        // Preserve replay-before-sniff and keep filesystem I/O off the writer.
        let sniffed = if file.is_none() { Some(snapback4_core::assets::sniff(&body)?) } else { None };
        let content_type = if file.is_some() { Some(snapback4_core::assets::verify_file(&body, declared.as_deref())?) } else { None };
        let (principal_check, facts_check, bytes) = (principal.clone(), facts.clone(), body.len() as u64);
        let upload = shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {
            crate::serve::session_identity::mutation_authority(&facts_check, shared, engine, &principal_check).map_err(|why| snapback4_core::RuntimeError::Auth(why.message))?;
            if let Some(name) = &file {
                engine.prepare_file(&principal_check, content_type.unwrap(), name, bytes, shared.now())
            } else { engine.prepare_asset(&principal_check, sniffed.unwrap(), bytes, shared.now()) }
        })?;
        #[cfg(test)] crate::serve::test_work(&shared.upload_work);
        let upload = if let Some(id) = &intent { upload.with_intent(id, &fingerprint).with_placement(placement.unwrap()) } else { upload };
        let upload = upload.write(&body)?;
        principal_of(&request, shared).map_err(|_| snapback4_core::RuntimeError::Auth("sign in again".into()))?;
        let principal = principal.clone();
        shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {
            crate::serve::session_identity::mutation_authority(&facts, shared, engine, &principal).map_err(|why| snapback4_core::RuntimeError::Auth(why.message))?;
            if let Some(expected) = &expected_store {
                if engine.store().store_identity()?.as_ref() != Some(expected) { return Err(snapback4_core::RuntimeError::Structural {code:"E_STORE_REPLACED",message:"upload store changed during disk write".into()}); }
            }
            engine.finish_asset(upload)
        })
    })();
    match stored {
        Ok(asset) => {
            let mut facts = json!({ "id": asset.id, "type": asset.content_type, "bytes": asset.bytes, "width": asset.width, "height": asset.height, "duration": asset.duration });
            if let Some(name) = asset.name { facts["name"] = json!(name); }
            respond(request, 200, json!({ "asset": facts }))
        }
        Err(error) => {
            let refusal = error.refusal();
            snapback4_core::diagnostic!("{} at POST /assets: {}", refusal.code, refusal.message);
            respond(request, if refusal.retryable { 503 } else { 200 }, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&refusal) }))
        }
    }
}

pub fn serve(request: Request, id: &str, shared: &Shared) {
    let (principal, _, scope) = match principal_of(&request, shared) {
        Ok(capability) => capability,
        Err(refusal) => return respond(request, 401, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&refusal) })),
    };
    if id.is_empty() || !id.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric()) {
        return respond(request, 404, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&Refusal::new("E_ASSET_UNKNOWN", "asset", "no asset is served under that id to this viewer").guide("assets")) }));
    }
    let _transfer = shared.asset_transfers.enter(id, &principal);
    if request.is_aborted() { return request.abort(); }
    let range_requested = request.headers().iter().any(|h| h.field.equiv("range"));
    let (facts, owned_principal, owned_id) = (RequestFacts::capture(&request), principal.clone(), id.to_owned());
    let granted = shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {
        crate::serve::session_identity::persona_read_authority(&facts, shared, engine)?;
        Ok::<_, Refusal>(engine.asset_access_request(&owned_principal, &owned_id, shared.now(), range_requested))
    });
    let granted = match granted { Ok(value) => value, Err(why) => return respond(request, 401, json!({"denied":why})) };
    let grant = match granted {
        Ok(grant) => grant,
        Err(error) => {
            let refusal = error.refusal();
            let status = match refusal.code.as_str() {
                "E_ASSET_VIEWED" => 410,
                "E_ASSET_RANGE" => 416,
                "E_ASSET_UNKNOWN" => 404,
                _ if refusal.retryable => 503,
                _ => 500,
            };
            return respond(request, status, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&refusal) }));
//! Values on the wire are plain JSON: ids and text are strings, numbers are
//! numbers, rows are objects. The typed form (`Value`) is recovered from an
//! argument's declared type, so a device never spells a tag.

use crate::ir::ArgType;
use crate::value::Value;
use serde_json::{Map, Value as Json};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

/// Additive acquisition markers, ordered before `events[at]` (or after the
/// last event). No floor starts acquisition; a floor completes it. `whole`
/// proves the group end; a keyed completion uses a delivered current readable
/// selected key, never a withheld historical key. No safe key leaves it unfinished.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Acquisition {
    pub at: usize,
    pub table: String,
    pub index: String,
    pub group: Vec<serde_json::Value>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub floor: Option<String>,
}

/// Audience prefixes only, keyed by delivered-history table. An empty list
/// means this principal currently holds none of that table’s groups.
pub type HeldGroups = BTreeMap<String, Vec<Vec<Json>>>;

/// Serialize a borrowed value directly in its plain wire form, without
/// allocating an intermediate JSON tree. The tagged store form is unchanged.
pub struct Plain<'a>(pub &'a Value);

impl serde::Serialize for Plain<'_> {
    fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        match self.0 {
            Value::Null => serializer.serialize_unit(),
            Value::Bool(value) => serializer.serialize_bool(*value),
            Value::Int(value) => serializer.serialize_i64(*value),
            Value::String(value) | Value::Id(value) => serializer.serialize_str(value),
            Value::Bytes(value) => serializer.serialize_str(&crate::value::encode_bytes_hex(value)),
            Value::Array(values) => serializer.collect_seq(values.iter().map(Plain)),
            Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => serializer.collect_map(fields.iter().map(|(key, value)| (key, Plain(value)))),
        }
    }
}

pub fn to_json(value: &Value) -> Json {
    match value {
        Value::Null => Json::Null,
        Value::Bool(b) => Json::Bool(*b),
        Value::Int(n) => Json::Number((*n).into()),
        Value::String(s) | Value::Id(s) => Json::String(s.clone()),
        Value::Bytes(bytes) => Json::String(crate::value::encode_bytes_hex(bytes)),
        Value::Array(items) => Json::Array(items.iter().map(to_json).collect()),
        Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => Json::Object(map_to_json(fields)),
    }
}

/// A plain JSON argument as the typed value its declaration names.
pub fn from_json(kind: &ArgType, json: &Json) -> Result<Value, String> {
    Ok(match (kind, json) {
        (ArgType::Optional(_), Json::Null) => Value::Null,
        (ArgType::Optional(inner), other) => from_json(inner, other)?,
        (ArgType::Cursor, Json::Null) => Value::Null,
        (ArgType::Cursor, Json::String(s)) => Value::String(s.clone()),
        (ArgType::Id | ArgType::Principal | ArgType::Ref { .. }, Json::String(s)) => Value::Id(s.clone()),
        (ArgType::Text { .. } | ArgType::Enum { .. }, Json::String(s)) => Value::String(s.clone()),
        (ArgType::Bytes { .. }, Json::String(s)) => Value::Bytes(crate::value::decode_bytes_hex(s).ok_or("bytes must be lowercase base16")?),
        (ArgType::Int | ArgType::IntRange { .. } | ArgType::Time | ArgType::Decimal { .. } | ArgType::Money { .. }, Json::Number(n)) => Value::Int(n.as_i64().ok_or("an integer")?),
        (ArgType::Bool, Json::Bool(b)) => Value::Bool(*b),
        (ArgType::Json { .. } | ArgType::Scalar, other) => untyped(other)?,
        (ArgType::Image { .. } | ArgType::Video { .. } | ArgType::File { .. }, Json::Object(fields)) => asset_from_json(fields)?,
        (ArgType::List { of, .. } | ArgType::ListRange { of, .. }, Json::Array(items)) => Value::Array(items.iter().map(|item| match of { Some(of) => from_json(of, item), None => untyped(item) }).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?),
        (kind, other) => return Err(format!("expected {}, got {}", describe(kind), other_kind(other))),
    })
}

/// Decode one operation's wire object, resolving legacy argument aliases to
/// canonical bindings before the interpreter sees them.
pub fn arguments_from_json(program: &crate::ir::Program, json: &Json) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Value>, crate::RuntimeError> {
    decode_arguments(program, json, |_, message| crate::RuntimeError::Input(message))
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
pub fn arguments_from_json_with_refusal(program: &crate::ir::Program, json: &Json) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Value>, crate::error::Refusal> {
    decode_arguments(program, json, |kind, message| {
        crate::error::Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", message).guide(kind.guide())
    })
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum ArgumentErrorKind {
    Program,
    Type,
}

impl ArgumentErrorKind {
    fn guide(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Program => "programs",
            Self::Type => "types",
        }
    }
}

fn decode_arguments<E>(program: &crate::ir::Program, json: &Json, error: impl Fn(ArgumentErrorKind, String) -> E) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Value>, E> {
    let fields = json.as_object().ok_or_else(|| error(ArgumentErrorKind::Program, "args must be an object".into()))?;
    for (alias, canonical) in &program.arg_aliases {
        if fields.contains_key(alias) && fields.contains_key(canonical) {
            return Err(error(ArgumentErrorKind::Program, format!("{} received both argument {canonical} and its alias {alias}; send exactly one", program.name)));
        }
    }
    let mut typed = BTreeMap::new();
    for (wire_name, value) in fields {
        let (canonical, kind) = program.argument(wire_name).ok_or_else(|| error(ArgumentErrorKind::Program, format!("{} takes no argument {wire_name}", program.name)))?;
        let decoded = from_json(kind, value).map_err(|why| error(ArgumentErrorKind::Type, format!("argument {wire_name}: {why}")))?;
        typed.insert(canonical.to_owned(), decoded);
    }
    Ok(typed)
}

#[test]
fn browse_matches_bucket_duration_and_offset_not_only_column_names() {
    let source = "table t:\n  owner: id\n  at: time\n  body: text <=40\n  by aWrongPeriod: owner, bucket(at, 2h), at, id\n  by bWrongOffset: owner, bucket(at, 1h, 30m), at, id\n  by zBrowse: owner, bucket(at, 1h), at, id\n  by byWords: owner, bucket(at, 1h), words(body), at, id\n  public 't'\nquery page(owner: id, q: text <=40, c: cursor ?):\n  return t[owner, 0] matching q first 1 by byWords after c\n";
    for wrong in ["aWrongPeriod", "bWrongOffset"] {
        // Each different calendar identity competes under the exact same names.
        let omit = if wrong == "aWrongPeriod" { "  by bWrongOffset: owner, bucket(at, 1h, 30m), at, id\n" } else { "  by aWrongPeriod: owner, bucket(at, 2h), at, id\n" };
        let b = bound(&source.replace(omit, ""));
        assert_eq!(b.schema.tables["t"].indexes[wrong].columns(), b.schema.tables["t"].indexes["zBrowse"].columns());
        let browse = scans(&b.programs[0].program).into_iter().find(|s| !s.prefix.iter().any(|k| matches!(k, IndexKeyExpr::WordPrefix(_)))).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(browse.index, "zBrowse");
        let mut e = Engine::memory(b.schema, b.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
        e.seed([0, 1_800_000, 3_599_999, 3_600_000].into_iter().enumerate().map(|(n, at)| ("t".into(), object([("id", id(&n.to_string())), ("owner", id("alice")), ("at", Value::Int(at)), ("body", text("word"))])))).unwrap();
        for q in ["", "word"] {
            assert_eq!(page_ids(&mut e, "page", BTreeMap::from([("owner".into(), id("alice")), ("q".into(), text(q))])), [id("0"), id("1"), id("2")]);
        }
    }
}
#[test]
fn every_planned_page_keeps_nullable_unique_ties_and_explicit_unsafe_cursors_refuse() {
    let table = "table t:\n  owner: id\n  at: time ?\n  unique byOwnerAt: owner, at\n  public 't'\n";
    for existing in [false, true] {
        for direction in ["first", "last"] {
            let table = if existing { table.replace("  public", "  by byTime: owner, at, id\n  public") } else { table.into() };
            let source = format!("{table}view v:\n  t {{ owner, at }}\nquery predicate(owner: id, c: cursor ?):\n  return t where .owner = owner {direction} 1 by .at after c\nquery named(owner: id, c: cursor ?):\n  return t[owner = owner] {direction} 1 by .at after c\nquery values(owner: id, c: cursor ?):\n  return t where .owner in [owner] {direction} 1 by .at after c\nquery projected(owner: id, c: cursor ?):\n  return v where .owner = owner {direction} 1 by .at after c\n");
            let b = bound(&source);
            for p in &b.programs { for scan in scans(&p.program) {
                assert_eq!(b.schema.tables["t"].indexes[&scan.index].columns(), ["owner", "at", "id"]);
                assert_ne!(scan.index, "byOwnerAt");
            } }
            let mut e = Engine::memory(b.schema, b.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
            e.seed(["a", "b"].into_iter().map(|n| ("t".into(), object([("id", id(n)), ("owner", id("alice")), ("at", Value::Null)])))).unwrap();
            for name in ["predicate", "named", "values", "projected"] {
                let mut expected = vec![id("a"), id("b")]; if direction == "last" { expected.reverse(); }
                assert_eq!(page_ids(&mut e, name, BTreeMap::from([("owner".into(), id("alice"))])), expected);
            }
        }
    }
    let source = format!("{table}query unsafePage(owner: id, c: cursor ?):\n  return t[owner] first 1 by byOwnerAt after c\n");
    let b = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source)]);
    let d = b.diagnostics.iter().find(|d| d.code == "E_CURSOR_INDEX").unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{:?}", b.diagnostics));
    assert!(d.message.contains("nullable") && d.rewrite.contains("by .at"), "{d:?}");
    let rewritten = bound(&format!("{table}query safePage(owner: id, c: cursor ?):\n  return {}\n", d.rewrite));
    let unique = &rewritten.schema.tables["t"].indexes["byOwnerAt"];
    assert!(unique.unique); assert_eq!(unique.columns(), ["owner", "at"]);
}
#[test]
fn nullable_unique_cursor_rewrite_preserves_computed_key_definitions() {
    for component in ["hour(at)", "bucket(at, 2h, 30m)"] {
        let table = format!("table t:\n  owner: principal ?\n  at: time\n  unique byPeriod: owner, {component}\n  public 't'\n");
        let source = format!("{table}query q(c: cursor ?):\n  return t[viewer] first 1 by byPeriod after c\n");
        let b = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source)]);
        let d = b.diagnostics.iter().find(|d| d.code == "E_CURSOR_INDEX").unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{:?}", b.diagnostics));
        let forms: Vec<_> = d.rewrite.split('`').collect();
        assert_eq!(forms.len(), 5, "{d:?}");
        let fixed = bound(&format!("{}query q(c: cursor ?):\n  return {}\n", table.replace("  public", &format!("  {}\n  public", forms[1])), forms[3]));
        let indexes = &fixed.schema.tables["t"].indexes;
        assert!(indexes["byPeriod"].unique);
        assert!(!indexes["byPeriodPage"].unique);
        assert_eq!(&indexes["byPeriodPage"].components[..2], indexes["byPeriod"].components.as_slice());
        assert_eq!(indexes["byPeriodPage"].columns().last().unwrap(), "id");
    }
}
const WORK: &str = "effect notify\ntable t:\n  n: int\n  cap 10\n  public 't'\n  update <- allow\n  sync public\n";
#[test]
fn presence_domains_refuse_population_loops_with_an_ordinary_loop_rewrite() {
    let optional = "t where (status = null or .n = status) first 1 by .id after c";
    for domain in [optional, "t first 1 by .id after c"] {
        let source = format!("{WORK}mutation send(status: int ?, c: cursor ?):\n  for row in {domain}:\n    emit notify {{ id: row.id }}\n");
        let b = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source)]);
        assert!(b.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT"), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    }
    let alias = format!("{WORK}mutation send(status: int ?, c: cursor ?):\n  page = {optional}\n  for row in page:\n    emit notify {{ id: row.id }}\n");
    let b = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), alias)]);
    assert!(b.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT"), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    let b = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!("{WORK}job sweep(status: int ?):\n  for row in t where (status = null or .n = status):\n    update t[row.id] {{ n: 9 }}\n"))]);
    assert!(b.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_PLACEMENT" && d.message.contains("argument-presence") && d.rewrite.contains("inside")), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
}

// ---- #7: a unique-key equality is a bound; a covering bound needs no cursor ----

#[test]
fn a_pinned_unique_key_bounds_a_page_and_needs_no_cursor() {
    let schema = "table results:\n  challenge: text <= 40\n  winner: principal\n  unique challenge\n  public 'p'\n  online only\ntable subscriptions:\n  subscriber: principal\n  topic: enum('news', 'events', 'offers')\n  unique subscriber, topic\n  read <- .subscriber = viewer\n  insert <- .subscriber = viewer\n  online only\n";
    for query in [
        // 098: a unique key, at most one row.
        "query r(challenge: text):\n  return results where .challenge = challenge\n",
        // 058: the row's id.
        "query r(result: results):\n  return results where .id = result\n",
        // 041: a unique key over a three-value enum: three rows per subscriber.
        "query r():\n  return subscriptions where .subscriber = viewer\n",
        // A page at or above the bound needs no cursor either.
        "query r():\n  return subscriptions where .subscriber = viewer first 3 by .topic\n",
    ] {
        let source = format!("{schema}{query}");
        let b = clean(&source);
        assert!(note(&b, "N_NO_CURSOR").is_none(), "{source}\n{:#?}", b.notes);
    }
    // The bound is exact on the engine: every subscription comes back, complete.
    use snapback4_core::value::object;
    let b = clean(&format!("{schema}query r():\n  return subscriptions where .subscriber = viewer\n"));
    let mut engine = Engine::memory(b.schema, b.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
    let sub = |id: &str, topic: &str| ("subscriptions".to_owned(), object([("id", Value::Id(id.into())), ("subscriber", Value::Id("ann".into())), ("topic", Value::String(topic.into()))]));
    engine.seed([sub("s1", "news"), sub("s2", "events"), sub("s3", "offers")]).unwrap();
    let outcome = engine.query("r", Context::new("ann", args(&[]))).unwrap();
    assert!(outcome.complete && outcome.data.as_array().unwrap().len() == 3, "{outcome:?}");
    // A smaller page still notes the missing cursor, and a nullable key bounds nothing.
    assert!(note(&clean(&format!("{schema}query r():\n  return subscriptions where .subscriber = viewer first 2 by .topic\n")), "N_NO_CURSOR").is_some());
    let nullable = "table tags:\n  owner: principal\n  slug: text <= 40 ?\n  unique slug\n  public 'p'\n  online only\nquery r(slug: text):\n  return tags where .slug = slug\n";
    first(nullable, "E_QUARRY_BOUND");
}

/// Apply a read-hop rewrite to `table` the way an author would (the
/// wave-2 helper, for merged repairs too).
fn apply_hop_rewrite(source: &str, table: &str, rewrite: &str) -> String {
    let quoted: Vec<&str> = rewrite.split('`').skip(1).step_by(2).collect();
    let mut lines: Vec<String> = source.lines().map(str::to_owned).collect();
    let header = lines.iter().position(|l| l.starts_with(&format!("table {table}:"))).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no {table} in {source}"));
    let end = (header + 1..lines.len()).find(|&i| !lines[i].starts_with("  ")).unwrap_or(lines.len());
    let mut inserted = Vec::new();
    for piece in &quoted {
        if let Some(read) = piece.strip_prefix("read <- ") {
            let at = (header..end).find(|&i| lines[i].trim_start().starts_with("read <-")).expect("a read line");
            lines[at] = format!("  read <- {read}");
        } else if let Some(check) = piece.strip_prefix("insert <- … and ") {
            let at = (header..end).find(|&i| lines[i].trim_start().starts_with("insert <-")).expect("an insert line");
            lines[at] = format!("{} and {check}", lines[at]);
        } else if piece.starts_with("immutable ") {
            inserted.push(format!("  {piece}"));
        } else if piece.split_once(": ").is_some_and(|(name, ty)| name.chars().all(char::is_alphanumeric) && !ty.contains('[')) {
            inserted.push(format!("  {piece}"));

/// Decode one operation's wire object, resolving legacy argument aliases to
/// canonical bindings before the interpreter sees them.
pub fn arguments_from_json(program: &crate::ir::Program, json: &Json) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Value>, crate::RuntimeError> {
    decode_arguments(program, json, |_, message| crate::RuntimeError::Input(message))
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
pub fn arguments_from_json_with_refusal(program: &crate::ir::Program, json: &Json) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Value>, crate::error::Refusal> {
    decode_arguments(program, json, |kind, message| {
        crate::error::Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", message).guide(kind.guide())
    })
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum ArgumentErrorKind {
    Program,
    Type,
}

impl ArgumentErrorKind {
    fn guide(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Program => "programs",
            Self::Type => "types",
        }
    }
}

//! Bind key operands once, retaining authored sequencing and contextual literals.
use super::*;

impl<'a> Binder<'a> {
    pub(super) fn bind_key_parts(&mut self, info: &TableInfo, read: &ReadExpr, end: usize,
        keys: &mut Vec<(Option<String>, Expr, Ty)>, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<()> {
        for (position, part) in read.keys.iter().enumerate().take(end).skip(keys.len()) {
            let mut setup = setup::Body::default();
            let expected = part.column.as_deref().or_else(|| read.index.as_ref().and_then(|name| info.indexes.iter().find(|i| &i.name == name)).and_then(|i| i.columns.get(position)).map(String::as_str)).and_then(|column| key_identity(info, column));
            let (e, t) = match expected {
                Some(expected) => self.expr_as_reference(&part.value, &mut setup, &expected)?,
                None => self.expr(&part.value, &mut setup)?,
            };
            self.sequence_setup(keys.iter_mut().map(|(_, e, _)| e), setup, out);
            let e = if expr::allocates(&e) { self.snapshot(e, out) } else { e };
            keys.push((part.column.clone(), e, t));
        }
        self.contextualize_bound_keys(info, read, keys)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Apply the selected index's identity context to operands already bound
    /// for type-directed positional selection. This changes only their
    /// retained IR/type and never evaluates the authored expression again.
    pub(super) fn contextualize_bound_keys(&self, info: &TableInfo, read: &ReadExpr,
        keys: &mut [(Option<String>, Expr, Ty)]) -> Fallible<()> {
        if let Some(index) = read.index.as_ref().and_then(|name| info.indexes.iter().find(|i| &i.name == name)) {
            for (position,(column,value,ty)) in keys.iter_mut().enumerate() {

    pub(super) fn name_bound_keys(&mut self, info: &TableInfo, read: &ReadExpr,
        keys: &mut [(Option<String>, Expr, Ty)]) -> Fallible<()> {
        for ((column, expr, ty), part) in keys.iter_mut().zip(&read.keys) {

        else { Ty::from_scalar(info.columns.get(column)?) };
    ty.required().is_identity().then_some(ty)

//! index; the runtime, adoption and residency never distinguish its provenance.
use super::catalog::{Catalog, TableInfo};
use super::intent_walk as walk;

#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(super) struct Requests {

    errors: Vec<Diagnostic>,
    contexts: super::intent_aggregates::Contexts,
    /// Reads that are a merge's lanes (or planned as one): their order is
    /// the merge's shared order, so an equality on it stays a seek.
    merged: std::collections::BTreeSet<String>,
    lane: bool,
    pub(super) cap_repairs: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}

// @ref LLP 3000.013#2.1 — intrinsic id resolves every table-local tie.
// Normalize authored table reads before view expansion: a view's shared order
// must retain later keys because different branches can carry the same id.
pub(super) fn table_order(catalog: &mut Catalog) {
    let mut normalize = |value: &mut Expr| {
        if let Expr::Read(read) = value && read.matching.is_some() && read.index.is_some()
            && let Some(table) = catalog.tables.get(&read.table) {
            let original = read.clone();
            if super::intent_search::named_order(table, read) {
                let source = catalog.source.expression(&Expr::Read(original));
                catalog.read_origins.entry(read.site.to_string()).or_insert_with(|| source.clone());
                catalog.canonical_read_origins.entry(read.site.to_string()).or_insert(source);
            }
        }
        if let Expr::Read(read) | Expr::Exists { read, .. } = value
            && catalog.tables.contains_key(&read.table)
            && let Some(id) = read.order_keys.iter().position(|column| column == "id")
            && id + 1 < read.order_keys.len() {
            catalog.read_origins.entry(read.site.to_string()).or_insert_with(|| catalog.source.expression(&Expr::Read(read.clone())));
            catalog.canonical_read_origins.entry(read.site.to_string()).or_insert_with(|| if read.index.is_none() { crate::print::read_expr(read) } else { catalog.source.expression(&Expr::Read(read.clone())) });
            read.order_keys.truncate(id + 1);
        }
    };
    for doc in &mut catalog.documents {
        walk::document(doc, &mut normalize);
        for view in &mut doc.views {
            for branch in &mut view.branches {
                if let Some(predicate) = &mut branch.predicate { walk::expression(predicate, &mut normalize); }
                walk::shape(&mut branch.fields, &mut normalize);
            }
        }
    }
}

//! Compiler diagnostics describe authored sites, never generated index names.
use super::catalog::{Catalog, TableInfo};
use crate::{ast::IndexDecl, diag::Diagnostic};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

pub(super) fn authored(catalog: &Catalog, diagnostics: &mut [Diagnostic]) {
    // An identical definition has the same generated name on different tables.
    // Resolve the diagnostic's table before replacing an unqualified name.
    let mut indexes: BTreeMap<&str, Vec<(&TableInfo, &IndexDecl)>> = BTreeMap::new();
    for table in catalog.tables.values() {
        for index in table.indexes.iter().filter(|index| index.name.starts_with("$intent:")) {
            indexes.entry(&index.name).or_default().push((table, index));
        }
    }
    for diagnostic in diagnostics {
        for (name, candidates) in &indexes {
            if !diagnostic.message.contains(name) && !diagnostic.rewrite.contains(name) { continue; }
            let qualified = |table: &TableInfo| format!("{}.{}", table.decl.name, name);
            let by = |table: &TableInfo| format!("{} by {name}", table.decl.name);
            // N_NEVER_COMPLETE spells its page `table[..] by name`.
            let page = |table: &TableInfo| format!("{}[..] by {name}", table.decl.name);
            let selected = candidates.iter().find(|(table, _)| diagnostic.message.contains(&qualified(table)) || diagnostic.message.contains(&by(table)) || diagnostic.message.contains(&page(table)))
                .or_else(|| candidates.iter().find(|(_, index)| index.site == diagnostic.site));
            let description = selected.map(|(table, index)| label(table, index)).unwrap_or_else(|| candidates.iter().map(|(table, index)| label(table, index)).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" or "));
            if diagnostic.rewrite.contains(name) { diagnostic.mechanical = false; }
            // First replace qualified occurrences individually, even if one
            // diagnostic refers to identical definitions on several tables.
            for (table, index) in candidates {
                let target = label(table, index);
                diagnostic.message = diagnostic.message.replace(&page(table), &format!("{}[..] by {target}", table.decl.name)).replace(&qualified(table), &target).replace(&by(table), &target);
                diagnostic.rewrite = diagnostic.rewrite.replace(&qualified(table), &target);
            }
            diagnostic.message = diagnostic.message.replace(name, &description);
            if diagnostic.rewrite.contains(name) {
                let index = selected.unwrap_or(&candidates[0]).1;
                let order = index.columns.iter().map(|column| format!(".{column}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
                diagnostic.rewrite = diagnostic.rewrite.replace(&format!("by {name}"), &format!("by {order}")).replace(name, &description);
                // A generated name never appeared in source; it cannot be the
                // target of a spelling-only source repair.
                diagnostic.mechanical = false;
            }
        }
    }
}

fn label(table: &TableInfo, index: &IndexDecl) -> String {
    let unique = table.decl.indexes.iter().any(|decl| decl.name == index.name && decl.unique);
    format!("{} on {} ({}) at {}", if unique { "unique declaration" } else { "read or declaration" }, table.decl.name, index.columns.join(", "), index.site)
}

/// `check --emit-lean <file.q>`: one file, checked, as the Lean model's
/// schema, helpers and programs (`snapback4_lang::emit::lean`).
// @ref LLP 3000.035#52-stage-2-a-small-lean-core — the emitter's command-line face; the harness calls the library directly
fn emit_lean(file: &str) -> i32 {
    let source = match std::fs::read_to_string(file) {
        Ok(source) => source,
        Err(error) => { eprintln!("cannot read {file}: {error}"); return 2; }
    };
    let name = Path::new(file).file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()).unwrap_or(file).to_owned();
    match snapback4_lang::emit::lean::lean(&[(name, source)]) {
        Ok(module) => { println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&module.to_json()).unwrap()); 0 }
        Err(snapback4_lang::emit::lean::LeanError::Diagnostics(problems)) => {
            for problem in problems { eprintln!("{problem}"); }
            1
        }
        Err(snapback4_lang::emit::lean::LeanError::Unsupported(u)) => {
            eprintln!("outside the Lean model's fragment: {u}");
            1
        }
    }
}

pub fn check(options: &Options) -> i32 {
    if options.flags.contains_key("audit") { return security::audit(options); }
    if options.flags.contains_key("store") && options.flags.contains_key("release") {
        return releases::check_release(options);
    }

    if let Some(file) = options.flags.get("emit-lean") {
        return emit_lean(file);
    }
    let project = project_or_exit();
    let started = Instant::now();
    package_versions::warn(&project);
    upgrade_history::report(&project, options.json);
    if options.flags.contains_key("fix") {
        if let Err(code) = fix::checked(fix::compile(&project)) { return code; }
    }
    let compiled_sources = match project.sources() {
        Ok(sources) => sources,
        Err(error) => { eprintln!("cannot read snapback/: {error}"); return 2; }
    };
    let mut bound = phase::measure("check.bind", || snapback4_lang::compile(&compiled_sources));
    let reviewable_notes = bound.notes.iter().map(note_reviews::fingerprint).collect();
    for warning in saved_fixture_drift::warnings(&project) {
        if warning.drift { eprintln!("check: WARNING: saved fixture drift: {}", warning.message); }
        else { eprintln!("check: info: {}", warning.message); }

//! The Lean model's case format (LLP 3000.035 §5.2): a checked Quarry
//! program, translated from its **surface** syntax tree into the terms of
//! `snapback4/lean/Quarry/Syntax.lean`, as the JSON that
//! `snapback4/lean/Quarry/CaseJson.lean` decodes (format:
//! `snapback4/lean/README.md`, "The case format").
//!
//! **Why the surface tree.** The model is a second implementation of the
//! binder and the interpreter together. Reading the binder's IR would copy
//! the binder's decisions into the model's input, and the comparison could
//! no longer find a binder defect. The input is the parsed [`Document`]s.
//! Besides the fact that [`crate::compile`] reported no diagnostics, the case
//! carries the checked schema's selected plain expiry-index columns: that
//! physical choice determines observable cross-root action order and the
//! across-call continuation tuple. The emitter independently selects the first
//! eligible catalog entry; this qualifies execution given the planned index
//! catalog, not the planner's index synthesis. No program IR is read.
//!
//! **Types.** The few places that need a type (a text literal beside an id is
//! an id, OPEN V1; a positional key chooses a unique key by its argument
//! types, indexes card) take it from the surface's own declarations, which
//! the type checker has accepted: column types, argument types, helper
//! parameters, `viewer : principal`, and literal kinds, propagated through
//! locals by the small inference in [`Scope::ty`]. When that inference cannot
//! decide, the program is unsupported, never guessed.
//!
//! **The expansions** are those `Syntax.lean` documents: `public` is
//! `read <- allow`; an omitted rule is `deny`; an unnamed `update <- R` is
//! `R[old] and R[next]` (OPEN R2); positional keys become named equalities
//! on `id` (an `id`-typed or `t`-typed single key) or on the one declared
//! unique key whose column types accept the arguments in order; in a
//! `where`, each `.col = e` conjunct (e not reading the row) is a pin and the
//! remaining conjuncts are the filter; `return insert …` is a bound write
//! followed by `return`.
//!
//! **Residency.** Sync presence is retained for private exhaustion admission;
//! device holding details are omitted. Read-through tables are explicitly
//! unsupported. Non-unique `by` indexes are erased (tuning; reads choose
//! indexes themselves). A `text <= N`
//! bound is not modelled as a value restriction (OPEN W6):
//! [`LeanModule::store`] and [`LeanModule::tag_args`] refuse inputs that exceed
//! it, and a literal written past it is unsupported. The surface emitter does
//! use the bound to keep PAGE cases with nonportable synthesized keys out of
//! the fragment before the oracle. A computed text written to a bounded column
//! is not checked.
//!
//! **Everything else** outside the model's core fragment is an
//! [`Unsupported`] with a stable `reason` (counted by the harness, never a
//! pass) and a `detail` naming the construct. A translation is all or
//! nothing: there is no partial program.

/// A construct outside the model's core fragment.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]
pub struct Unsupported {
    /// Stable, low-cardinality name (the harness counts by it).
    pub reason: String,
    /// The construct, for a human.
    pub detail: String,
}

impl Unsupported {
    fn new(reason: impl Into<String>, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { reason: reason.into(), detail: detail.into() }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Unsupported {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "{}: {}", self.reason, self.detail)
    }
}

## 2026-10-27 — OWN review fixes: bounded diagnostics and serving-only G6 exit

The first OWN implementation could wedge before publishing loss when stderr
stalled, and armed its G6 process exit for short-lived deploy before activation
reconciliation. Loss now precedes bounded diagnostic queueing; queued replies
drain without logging I/O, and exit allows at most 100 ms for diagnostic output.
Only `serving()` arms the G6 exit. Deploy retains persisted-selection recovery,
pointer/log completion and lease release. The report's new regressions fill a
real stderr pipe and delay an unknown-but-durable activation's reconciliation
probe. LLP 3000.009.001.000 §5.1 records the corrected lifecycle contract.

## 2026-10-27 — CALLS1: image metadata and a quiet install join

Wave 34 file options selected the document path on image-only schemas. The client now retries only the explicit pre-body no-file-column refusal through the existing media sniffer, using the same bytes and credentials; mixed/file schemas keep document semantics. Image bounds, placement and authorization remain enforced. The installer retains its private worker custody, puts npm chatter in its private log and gives --wait one final completion line; init promotes that blocking join instead of status polling. No version bump.

CALLS1's explicitly requested MIME/name/size upload shape adds only optional advisory `UploadOptions.file.size`; the server still measures the bytes and the existing result/authority contract is unchanged. This is the scoped upload option acceptance authorized by the brief, not a client-contract redesign.

//! Refusals: every failure the engine reports is one envelope
//! `{code, family, site, message, rewrite, guide}` (LLP 2000.000 §5.1), and
//! the same envelope is what a device shows and what `why` explains.

use crate::schema::Effect;
use crate::value::ValueError;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use thiserror::Error;

/// The refusal envelope. `code` and `family` are stable identifiers; `rewrite`
/// is text the author can paste; `guide` is the keyword card to read.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Refusal {
    pub code: String,
    pub family: String,
    pub message: String,
    /// Original constraint text for live development refusals; durable receipts and replays omit this row-derived detail.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub detail: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub site: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub rewrite: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub guide: Option<String>,
    /// The author's own code, for `require` and named unique refusals.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub rule: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")]
    pub retryable: bool,
}

impl Refusal {
    pub fn new(code: impl Into<String>, family: impl Into<String>, message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { code: code.into(), family: family.into(), message: message.into(), detail: None, site: None, rewrite: None, guide: None, rule: None, retryable: false }
    }
    pub fn site(mut self, site: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.site = Some(site.into());
        self
    }
    pub fn rewrite(mut self, rewrite: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.rewrite = Some(rewrite.into());
        self
    }
    pub fn guide(mut self, guide: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.guide = Some(guide.into());
        self
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Refusal {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "{}: {}", self.code, self.message)?;
        if let Some(site) = &self.site {
            write!(f, " (at {site})")?;
        }
        if let Some(rewrite) = &self.rewrite {
            write!(f, "\n  rewrite: {rewrite}")?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Which meter cut a program (LLP 2000.000 §6).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum MeterKind {
    Examined,
    IndexEntries,
    RuleProbes,
    Steps,
    HeapBytes,
    OutputBytes,
    RowsWritten,
}

impl MeterKind {
    pub fn word(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Examined => "examined rows",
            Self::IndexEntries => "index entries",
            Self::RuleProbes => "rule probes",
            Self::Steps => "steps",
            Self::HeapBytes => "heap bytes",
            Self::OutputBytes => "output bytes",
            Self::RowsWritten => "rows written",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum RuntimeError {
    /// The member is durable; its synchronous follow-up failed. Display and
    /// refusal policy stay those of the original error for existing callers.
    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    #[error(transparent)]
    Continuation(Box<RuntimeError>),
    #[cfg(feature = "server-search")]
    #[error("E_SEARCH_OPEN: {memberships} authorized membership keys discovered{unfinished}; opening exceeded this read's envelope ({ceiling} {resource} maximum) at {site}; use the grouped form in `snapback4 guide search`")]

/// A 204 has no representation metadata or advertised bytes. Keeping it out
/// of the JSON response helper also prevents an unread `null` from framing the
/// next response on a persistent connection.
pub(crate) fn respond_empty(request: Request, status: u16) {
    let mut response = Response::empty(status);
    if let Some(header)=generation_header(){response.add_header(header);}
    for header in cors(&request).into_iter().chain(latency::header()).filter(|header| !header.field.equiv("Content-Type")) {
        response.add_header(header);
    }
    let _ = request.respond(response);
}

pub(crate) fn refusal_json(refusal: &Refusal) -> Json {
    serde_json::to_value(refusal).unwrap_or(Json::Null)
}

pub fn check(options: &Options) -> i32 {
    if options.flags.contains_key("audit") { return security::audit(options); }
    if options.flags.contains_key("store") && options.flags.contains_key("release") {
        return releases::check_release(options);
    }

    if let Some(file) = options.flags.get("emit-lean") {
        return emit_lean(file);
    }
    let project = project_or_exit();
    let started = Instant::now();
    package_versions::warn(&project);
    upgrade_history::report(&project, options.json);
    if options.flags.contains_key("fix") {
        if let Err(code) = fix::checked(fix::compile(&project)) { return code; }
    }
    let compiled_sources = match project.sources() {
        Ok(sources) => sources,
        Err(error) => { eprintln!("cannot read snapback/: {error}"); return 2; }
    };
    let mut bound = phase::measure("check.bind", || snapback4_lang::compile(&compiled_sources));
    let reviewable_notes = bound.notes.iter().map(note_reviews::fingerprint).collect();
    for warning in saved_fixture_drift::warnings(&project) {
        if warning.drift { eprintln!("check: WARNING: saved fixture drift: {}", warning.message); }
        else { eprintln!("check: info: {}", warning.message); }
    }
    if options.flags.contains_key("fix") && bound.diagnostics.is_empty() {
        if let Err(error) = fix_fixtures::run(&project, &bound, options) { failed_check(&bound, options.json, "E_INPUT", format!("check --fix: {error}")); return 2; }
    }

    if let Some(hint) = project.saved_copy_hint() { if options.json { eprintln!("check: {hint}"); } else { println!("check: {hint}"); } }
    if let Some(error) = crate::exact_device::inspect(&project.root, &bound.schema).into_iter().find_map(Result::err) {
        if options.json { println!("{}", json!({"ok": false, "denied": {"code": "E_DEVICE_VERSION", "message": error}, "notes": bound.notes, "newNotes": bound.notes, "acknowledgedNotes": []})); }
        else { eprintln!("{error}"); }
        return 1;

    pub(crate) fn admit_checked(&mut self, mut entry: Queued, replay_candidate: bool, _identified: bool) -> Result<Queued, RuntimeError> {
        // @ref LLP 3000.017#4.5 — memory writes never enter durable admission or replay.
        if self.schema.operations.get(&entry.op).is_some_and(|f| f.ephemeral) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_QUARRY_EPHEMERAL", message: "ephemeral writes cannot enter the device outbox; call the online ephemeral lane".into() });
        }
        let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.4 — recheck adoption under the admission writer lock, after the SDK's final identity read.
        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
        if (_identified || entry.upload.is_some()) && tx.meta(BACKEND_REQUIRED)?.is_some_and(|value| !value.is_empty()) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_ADMISSION_STORE", message: "The backend needs adoption before this write can be admitted. Reload the current backend, then submit a new attempt.".into() });
        }
        store_identity::require_owner(&tx, &self.backend_identity, &self.store_identity, self.native_digest.as_deref())?;
        store_identity::require_healthy(&tx)?;
        if entry.upload.is_some() && tx.meta(BACKEND_REQUIRED)?.is_some_and(|s|!s.is_empty()){return Err(RuntimeError::Structural{code:"E_ADMISSION_STORE",message:"adopt the identified backend before admitting an upload".into()});}
        if let Some(upload) = entry.upload.as_mut() {
            if upload.get("bytes").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).is_none() { return Err(RuntimeError::Input("upload admission needs the selected bytes".into())); }
            upload["original_args"] = entry.args.clone();
        }
        // @ref LLP 3000#6-the-simulators-invariants — at-most-once admission compares under the store's writer transaction, before any speculative row or id changes.
        if let Some(data) = tx.outbox_get(&entry.id)? {
            let original: Queued = decoded(&data)?;
            if original.op != entry.op || original.upload.as_ref().and_then(|u| u.get("original_args")).unwrap_or(&original.args) != entry.upload.as_ref().and_then(|u| u.get("original_args")).unwrap_or(&entry.args) || upload::input(&original) != upload::input(&entry) || original.viewer != entry.viewer {
                return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_WRITE_ID_REUSE", message: "write id already belongs to a different operation or arguments; retry the original input or use a new id".into() });
            }
            tx.rollback()?;
            return Ok(original);
        }
        if entry.upload.is_some() {
            let history: serde_json::Value=tx.meta("client:write-history")?.as_deref().map(decoded).transpose()?.unwrap_or(serde_json::json!([]));
            if history.as_array().is_some_and(|items|items.iter().any(|w|w["id"]==entry.id)) {
                return Err(RuntimeError::Structural {code:"E_WRITE_ID_REUSE",message:"this upload id already settled; inspect its retained receipt before another admission".into()});
            }
        }
        let program = self.programs.get(&entry.op);
        match program {
            Some(program) if program.kind == snapback4_core::ProgramKind::Action && !replay_candidate => return Err(RuntimeError::UnknownOp("an action cannot enter the device outbox; call client.act".into())),
            None if !replay_candidate => return Err(RuntimeError::UnknownOp(entry.op.clone())),
            _ => {}
        }
        entry.seq = entry.seq.max(tx.outbox_max_seq()?.max(meta_u64(&tx, SUBMISSION)?) + 1);
        entry.predictable &= program.is_some_and(|p| p.kind == snapback4_core::ProgramKind::Mutation);
        if entry.upload.is_some() { upload::validate(&tx, &mut entry, &self.programs)?; entry.predictable = false; }
        if entry.predictable {
            tx.savepoint("admit")?;
            match predictions::run_with_minter(&tx, &self.schema, program.unwrap(), &entry, self.minter.clone()) {
                Ok((predicted, new_ids)) => {
                    entry.predicted = predicted;
                    entry.new_ids = new_ids;
                    entry.predictable = true;
                    tx.release("admit")?;
                }
                Err(error) if matches!(error, RuntimeError::Prediction(_)) || (replay_candidate && error.is_refusal()) => {
                    tx.rollback_to("admit")?;
                    entry.predictable = false;
                    entry.predicted.clear();
                }
                Err(error) => return Err(error),
            }
        }
        tx.outbox_insert(entry.seq, &entry.id, &encoded(&entry)?)?;
        tx.set_meta(SUBMISSION, &entry.seq.to_string())?;
        // Admission's time survives settlement in the same durable commit as
        // its outbox entry, including synchronous web journal recovery.
        keep_issued_floor(&tx, entry.now)?;
        self.preserved = Some(tx.change_footprint().preserved(&self.schema));
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok(entry)
    }

    /// The server answered a write: sent at `seq` (the entry waits for the

    /// survivors are replayed over the confirmed images.
    pub fn settle(&mut self, id: &str, seq: Option<u64>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.settle_from(id, seq, None)
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.023#11 — a late success belongs to the dispatching store.
